distributions.source: profile laundromat (ASSUMPTION): Replace with supplier quotes.

distributions.description: marketing cost as a share of revenue

distributions.description: maintenance cost as a share of revenue

distributions.source: profile laundromat (ASSUMPTION): Equipment repair; replace with the machine maker's service quote.

distributions.description: Paid staff hours per month
distributions.name: paid_hours_per_month
distributions.source: profile laundromat labor.paid_hours_per_month (ASSUMPTION): Zero for an unattended store; founder's staffing plan.

distributions.description: Hourly wage
distributions.name: hourly_wage
distributions.source: data fabric local_wages (ASSUMPTION): the profile's ASSUMPTION range scaled by the SYNTHETIC city's index (wage index 1.178); SYNTHETIC city generator (src/uwcopilot/studio/data/synthetic_city.py); derived with: profile labor.hourly_wage is an ASSUMPTION: Replace with BLS QCEW average weekly wage for NAICS 812310 in the metro (hours conversion stated) or BLS OEWS laundry workers for the metro.

distributions.description: Rent in the first year
distributions.name: monthly_rent
distributions.source: data fabric commercial_rent (ASSUMPTION): the profile's ASSUMPTION range scaled by the SYNTHETIC city's index (rent index 1.082); a founder's quote replaces it; SYNTHETIC city generator (src/uwcopilot/studio/data/synthetic_city.py); derived with: profile rent.monthly_rent is an ASSUMPTION: No free commercial-rent source. The founder's quote comes first; otherwise a metro range with a cited listing survey if one is found.

distributions.description: Rent increase each year
distributions.name: rent_escalation
distributions.source: profile laundromat rent (ASSUMPTION): Replace with the lease's escalation clause. A lease shorter than the equipment's life is a key risk.

distributions.description: Price elasticity of demand
distributions.name: price_elasticity
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): No public source identified for these business types and sites; calibrate from the founder's price tests or outcome data (S9).
distributions.unit: % fall in volume per 1% price rise, relative to the profile's reference price

distributions.description: Month-to-month demand noise
distributions.name: monthly_noise_sd
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): Replace with the spread of the founder's own monthly sales (or comparable sites') once a history exists.
distributions.unit: standard deviation of log monthly demand around its expected level

distributions.description: Payroll taxes and benefits
distributions.name: payroll_burden_share
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): Replace with the founder's payroll provider quote (taxes depend on the state and the benefits offered).
distributions.unit: payroll taxes and benefits as a share of wages

distributions.description: Build-out overrun
distributions.name: capex_overrun_share
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): Replace with the contingency line of the founder's contractor bids.
distributions.unit: build-out overrun as a share of the planned build-out and equipment cost

distributions.description: Chance per year that a competitor opens nearby
distributions.name: competitor_entry_annual_probability
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): Replace with new-establishment counts for the industry in the metro (Census Business Patterns year-over-year) once a snapshot has them. The mode is moved by the site's competition percentile (see setup.py).; mode set from the site's competition percentile 0.24 (a less saturated area is assumed to attract more entrants; a design choice)
distributions.unit: probability per year that a same-type competitor opens in the trade area

distributions.description: Demand lost after a competitor opens
distributions.name: competitor_entry_demand_loss
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): No public source identified; calibrate from outcome data (S9).
distributions.unit: share of demand lost from the month a competitor opens

distributions.description: Chance per year that the note rate rises
distributions.name: rate_shock_annual_probability
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): A planning range, not a rate forecast. Replace with the lender's own rate scenarios.
distributions.unit: probability per year that the note rate of a variable-rate loan rises (no effect on a fixed-rate loan)

distributions.description: Size of a rate rise
distributions.name: rate_shock_size_pct_points
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): A planning range, not a rate forecast. The lender stress preset separately applies the guideline's own +2.00 points (NBC-4.5).
distributions.unit: percentage points added to the note rate when a rate shock happens

distributions.description: Chance per year of a one-off repair, closure or vacancy
distributions.name: one_off_shock_annual_probability
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): No public source identified; replace with equipment-maker downtime data or the founder's insurance quote.
distributions.unit: probability per year of a one-off repair, closure or vacancy event

distributions.description: Revenue lost in the month of a one-off event
distributions.name: one_off_shock_revenue_loss_share
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): No public source identified; calibrate from outcome data (S9).
distributions.unit: share of that month's revenue lost in the month of the event

distributions.description: Repair bill of a one-off event, as a share of capex
distributions.name: one_off_shock_repair_cost_share_of_capex
distributions.source: config/studio/feasibility/assumptions.yaml (ASSUMPTION): Replace with the equipment maker's service quote or the founder's insurance deductible.
distributions.unit: repair bill as a share of the planned build-out and equipment cost

loan.rate_source: prime rate 6.25% (SYNTHETIC: SYNTHETIC prime rate of the generated city; NOT a published rate) + 3.0 points (spread is the ASSUMPTION mode (Not a lender quote. Replace with the lender's term sheet; the founder can type the quoted rate instead.))

result.metro_mode_reason: SYNTHETIC metro: generated data for demonstration and validation only
result.seasonality_source: profile laundromat seasonality (ASSUMPTION): Nearly flat is still an assumption, not a neutral default. Replace with the founder's or a seller's history.
shocks: competitor entry: at most once per path; its month follows a constant monthly hazard from the annual probability; demand is lower by the sampled loss from that month on
rate shock (variable-rate loans only): at most once per path; the remaining balance is re-amortized over the remaining term at the higher rate
one-off repair, closure or vacancy: at most once per path; that month loses the sampled share of revenue and pays a repair bill (a share of the planned capex)

tornado.method: one input at a time set to its P10 and then its P90 on every path, all other draws held fixed (same seed); swing = |metric at P90 - metric at P10|; ranked by swing; one-at-a-time swings ignore interactions between inputs
tornado.metric: year-2 net income (NOI minus debt service), P50 across paths, USD
